clue.text: Reasonable series covering grand amusement park

indicators.note: the series word sits over or across the grand letter, which it is placed right up against

parts.note: a reasonable price or deal is a fair one
G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand pounds
a round is a series, as of talks or drinks

explanation.surface: A sensible run of events that takes in a grand theme park day out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' is a placement word only: grand's G sits snug against the series word, not inside it. A grand is British slang for a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent or travelling site of rides and stalls is a funfair site, the place of an amusement park.

clue.text: Unable to move quickly

explanation.definitionFit: The word means firmly fixed, as in stuck fast, and also rapidly, as in running fast.

clue.text: Undemonstrative character in charge on European mountain

parts.note: berg is a Germanic word for mountain, also used in English for a large floating mass of ice

explanation.surface: A cold-mannered person in command atop an Alpine peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold, reserved person who shows no feeling is called by this frozen image.

clue.text: See about the Italian's jacket

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to get something is to see or understand it
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: Take a look at that Italian man's coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' as understand, as in 'I get it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gilet is a sleeveless padded jacket or waistcoat.

clue.text: One making elegant speech, last in lady chapel

parts.note: an orator is a skilled public speaker

indicators.note: last in means the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A fine speaker is the final one in the lady chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lady chapel' looks like one phrase, a chapel to the Virgin Mary; it splits, 'lady' giving Y and 'chapel' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratory is a small chapel for private prayer.

clue.text: Just beginning, first of newcomers on slope

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: an ascent is an upward slope

explanation.surface: Novice skiers starting out on the slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is just coming into existence, so it is only starting.

clue.text: Rubbish mostly, in skip

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: tripe is slang for nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Most of the junk ends up in a builder's skip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skip' looks like a rubbish container, but it is the verb: to move lightly, as in tripping along.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip is to step lightly and nimbly, the same light movement as to skip.

clue.text: One having no illusions about top celebrities

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the A-list are the most famous stars

explanation.surface: A clear-eyed person discussing the stars at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist sees things as they are, a person free of illusions.

clue.text: After start of picnic, mention cup of tea?

indicators.note: after places the mention word behind the picnic letter
start of means the opening letter of the word picnic

parts.note: a reference is a mention

explanation.surface: Following a picnic someone suggests a brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cup of tea' looks literal beside the picnic, but means one's liking, as in 'not my cup of tea'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is one's cup of tea is what one likes, one's favoured choice.

clue.text: Truth of account supported by clergyman's office

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece supported by another sits above it

parts.note: a curacy is the post of a curate

explanation.surface: An honest report backed by a priest's department.
explanation.definitionFit: Accuracy is correctness, conformity with the facts, which is truthfulness.

clue.text: Run off with some gorgeous tea lady

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone eloping with a beautiful woman who serves the tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition was 'Run off', but that means flee; 'Run off with' is the phrase meaning take, so 'with' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off with something is to take it without permission, which is theft.

clue.text: Join business partner

definitions.meaning: to connect or link one thing with another, as a verb
a colleague or partner in a firm, as a noun

explanation.surface: An instruction to team up with a commercial colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means connect; as a noun it names a colleague or partner in a firm.

clue.text: Others treated by me in old people's place?

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Other residents cared for by me in a care facility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' sounds medical, fitting the care home, but it is the anagram signal, making RESTHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A residential home for elderly people who need care is a place for the old; the question mark marks a definition by description.

clue.text: Join military group close to castle

parts.note: a unit is a body of soldiers

indicators.note: close to here means the end of, so the final letter of castle is taken

explanation.surface: Enlisting with a regiment stationed near a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' reads as near, but it means the end of the word castle.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite things is to bring them together into one, a synonym of joining.

clue.text: Details of cabinet reshuffle?

definitions.meaning: the particulars or intricacies of a matter
a reshuffle sees ministers enter and leave the cabinet, those coming and going

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means fine points of a subject, and literally those arriving and leaving the government.

clue.text: Courageous heading off each evening

indicators.note: heading off means the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: knightly means chivalrous and brave, like a knight

explanation.surface: A brave soul setting off on a journey every evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like departing, but it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens every night happens each evening.

clue.text: One inside thanks girl for liqueur

indicators.note: inside means put within the next word

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
I is the Roman numeral one
Maria is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone thanks a girl for a drink after dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a brand of coffee liqueur.

clue.text: Hot snack to eat is prepared

indicators.note: food that is prepared is made ready, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A warm bite to eat is ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A grilled sandwich served warm is a typical hot snack.

clue.text: Fundamentally, a skill is required to pen article

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as animals are kept in a pen, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Writing a piece requires real ability, deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like writing, fitting 'article', but it means enclose, as a sheep pen does.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is so deep down is so in their basic nature, which is what fundamentally means.

clue.text: Hollow-cheeked witch, nuisance, turned up

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman or witch

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a drag is a bore or nuisance

explanation.surface: A gaunt old witch, a pest, appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads like arrived, but in a down answer it flips DRAG to GARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A haggard face looks gaunt and drawn, with hollow cheeks.

clue.text: Printing error involving husband working in violent windstorm

indicators.note: involving means including, so one piece is taken within the other

parts.note: a typo is a typing or printing mistake
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A typesetter's mistake about a spouse at work during a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A typhoon is a tropical cyclone of the western Pacific, a violent storm.

clue.text: Papers Lily forged, about perfect

parts.note: ID means identity papers

indicators.note: forged means faked or hammered into new shape, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone faked identity documents for a woman called Lily, about perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a scene of ideal peace and happiness, so the adjective means perfect.

clue.text: I'm finished with ordinary painting technique

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
past means over or finished
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: An artist declares the job done with a plain style of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is applying paint thickly so brush or knife marks stand out.

clue.text: Student's large money-spinner?

parts.note: an earner is something that brings in money

explanation.surface: A student's big profitable sideline.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone studying a subject or skill, a pupil.

clue.text: Follow the old lady's doctrine

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
the old lady is slang for one's mother, ma

explanation.surface: Abiding by mother's teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogma is a set of principles laid down as true by an authority, a doctrine.

clue.text: Visit Juliet? That's right, for macaroni

parts.note: to pop in is to make a brief visit
Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ay is an old or dialect word for yes, that's right

explanation.surface: Calling on Juliet - correct, swapped for pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'macaroni' is not pasta: an eighteenth-century macaroni was a dandy affecting continental fashions.
explanation.definitionFit: A popinjay is a vain, showily dressed man, which is what an eighteenth-century macaroni was.

clue.text: Wayfarer with small number on loco

parts.note: no is the short form of number
loco is slang for crazy, mad

explanation.surface: A traveller with a little number riding a locomotive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loco' looks like a railway engine but is the slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad wanders from place to place, a traveller on the road.

clue.text: Study occupied by a college administrator

indicators.note: occupied by means the first word has the next one living inside it

parts.note: a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: A study being used by a university official.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is a senior college or faculty officer in charge of discipline or a faculty.

clue.text: All agreed a sum union needs to get distributed

indicators.note: distributed means spread out or shared around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trade union's money must be shared out, and everyone concurs.
explanation.definitionFit: A decision that every person supports, with no dissent, is one all agreed on.

clue.text: Provides staff, English, for minister's house

parts.note: to man a post is to provide it with staff

explanation.surface: An English household supplying the servants for a clergyman's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is the residence provided for a minister, especially in Scottish Presbyterian churches.

clue.text: Border TV channel

definitions.meaning: an edge or margin of something
dated British slang for a television channel, as in switching to the other one

explanation.surface: A broadcaster serving the Scottish Borders region.
explanation.walkthrough: Older British speakers called a TV channel a 'side': 'what's on the other side?'
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an edge or margin, and in British slang a television channel.

clue.text: Unexpected ending in 'Londonderry Air', London music hall song

indicators.note: an unexpected arrangement is a surprising new order of the letters
ending in picks the final letter of the song's first word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A surprise finale to the Irish tune, followed by a Cockney favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpected' scrambles Y (the end of Londonderry) with AIR and LONDON. 'Any Old Iron' is a comic music hall song made famous by Harry Champion.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is a classic Cockney comic number from the Edwardian music hall stage.
